messages:
Mia: Heads-up — Acme wants to POC a new model variant for their analytics assistant. They've asked if we can host `cedar-xl-8b` with an int4 variant (q4_0) in Dedicated for latency-sensitive queries. Also asking about pricing delta and SOC2/KMS hints.

Jonah: Thanks. Do we have that model in our catalog yet or is this a fresh onboarding? Any sample prompt set they want to run?

Mia: It's not in our catalog. They provided a small eval set (20 queries) — mostly short retrieval-style prompts. I uploaded the eval to the sales drive: gs://acme-poc/evals/cedar_eval_v1.jsonl.

Eva: I can run a quick compatibility scan. Important questions: tokenizer compatibility (BPE vs SentencePiece), model file format (hf-pt / gguf), and whether the variant uses fused kernels. If they want int4 (q4_0) we need to verify our runtime supports that quantization path on their target GPU family.

Priya: Security side — Acme requires KMS-backed keys for model weights and customer data-at-rest, plus an answered security questionnaire. We can offer our Private control plane (VPC + KMS) for the POC. Need to confirm if they want weights stored in their S3 or our object store.

Marco: On pricing — Dedicated pricing varies by committed GPUs / vCPUs. For an 8B model with int4, throughput is usually higher, so we can offer a custom POC rate: 1-week discounted Dedicated slot + 3 days of engineering support. I'll draft numbers once we have expected token/sec.

Jonah: Eva — can you paste the quick scanner command you use? Sales wants a one-liner they can show the customer.

Eva: Sure. Quick local compatibility check (internal tool):

```
redwoodctl model check --source gs://acme-models/cedar-xl-8b/ --format hf-pt 
  --expected-tokenizer bpe --quant q4_0
```

It returns a short table: tokenizer ok / vocab mismatch / unsupported ops. If it flags fused-kernel ops, we need to route to a fallback kernel or recommend q4f16.

Mia: If the check shows unsupported ops, what's the customer-visible impact? Latency spike? Failed deploy?

Eva: Usually either failed deploy (we block) or we let it deploy but fall back to slower kernels — higher latency and higher cost. For POC we prefer to resolve incompatibilities first.

Priya: For the security questionnaire: I'll attach a template answer. We can commit to SOC2 and KMS for the POC; for production they may want an on-prem package. Also confirm whether Acme requires egress restrictions — we support VPC endpoints.

Mia: Acme asked about data retention: they need 30-day logs and then deletion. Can we configure that per-customer?

Marco: Yes, per-tenant retention is supported in Private and Dedicated; Console has retention policies. There's a small engineering checklist to enable it for the account.

Jonah: Next steps I'm proposing: 1) Eva runs `redwoodctl model check` against their artifact and posts the output. 2) Priya to start the security answers and flag any blockers. 3) Marco to draft a POC pricing + SOW. 4) Mia to sync calendar with Acme for a kickoff next week.

Eva: Running scan now, will paste results in ~15m.

deploy-bot: model-scan started for cedar-xl-8b (job id: job_20260321_0912). ETA ~12m.

Eva: Scan finished — quick summary:
- Tokenizer: bpe -> OK
- Model format: hf-pt -> OK
- Unsupported ops: 2 aten::group_norm calls flagged (may require fallback)
- Quant path q4_0: supported on A10 + H100 kernels, fallback to fp16 on older A40s.

Eva: Full output (trimmed):
```
[PASS] tokenizer: bpe
[PASS] format: hf-pt
[WARN] op: aten::group_norm (requires CPU fallback)
[PASS] quant-path: q4_0 (kernels available for A10/H100)
```

Mia: Good details. Acme's infra plan is A10-based Dedicated, so q4_0 should be okay. The group_norm warning — regression risk?

Eva: Group_norm on CPU fallback may add 5-15ms per request depending on batch size. For short queries it's noticeable. Recommend either: 1) a small model patch to replace group_norm or 2) use q4f16 variant if they accept slightly higher memory.

Marco: I'll include both options in the SOW: engineering work estimate for the patch (2-3 days) vs recommending the q4f16 variant with throughput/latency numbers.

Priya: I also started the security questionnaire draft. One flag: Acme wants attestations for our kernel binaries — we can provide checksums and provenance, but full binary signing will be a follow-up enterprise ask. Flagging as "needs legal/Security OK" for now.

Mia: Thanks all. I'll update Acme: we'll propose Dedicated A10 POC with q4_0 supported, note the group_norm performance caveat and present the two remediation paths + pricing. Kickoff Wed 10am PT if that works.

Jonah: If Acme agrees, I'll schedule a brief tech deep-dive and send a checklist: sample payloads, expected QPS, and whether they want persistent KV caches enabled.

Mia: Perfect. I'll confirm time and loop in Acme.

Eva: Copy — I'll be on the deep-dive to walk through the scan and latency tradeoffs.

Priya: I will attach the partial security answers to the thread by EOD.

Marco: Draft SOW in my drive; sharing link in thread in a bit.

Mia: Thanks team :raised_hands:
